heading: Chap. ii.—I rejoice in your messengers.
paragraphs:
Since, then, I have
had the privilege of seeing
you, through Damas
your most worthy bishop,
and through your worthy
presbyters Bassus
and Apollonius, and
through my fellow-servant
the deacon Sotio,
whose friendship may I
ever enjoy, inasmuch as
he is subject to the
bishop as to the grace of
God, and to the presbytery
as to the law of
Jesus Christ, [I now
write[896] to you].

Since, then, I have had the
privilege of seeing you, through
Damas your most worthy[897] bishop,
and through your worthy[898] presbyters
Bassus and Apollonius, and
through my fellow-servant the
deacon Sotio, whose friendship may
I ever enjoy,[899] inasmuch as he, by
the grace of God, is subject to the
bishop and presbytery, in the law
of Jesus Christ, [I now write[900] to
you].
